title: tat tvam asi
tomorrow: two rivers run opposite ways. where do they both end up?

segments.voice: Yesterday the father said tat tvam asi at last, after a sleeper gone home and a bird that settles where it's tied. Shvetaketu asked for more. Today his father gives him bees.

The group project comes back with one grade. Somebody made the slides, somebody did the research, somebody stayed up fixing the ending. Now it's one thing, and it's hard to say whose sentence is whose. Honey works the same way. Ask a single drop which flower it came from, and there's no answer to give. That's the picture Uddalaka hands his son next.
screen: `ONE PROJECT, ONE GRADE.` → `WHOSE SENTENCE IS WHOSE?` → `ASK A DROP OF HONEY.`

segments.voice: Bees make honey, the father says, by gathering the juices of many kinds of trees and bringing them to one. In the honey, those juices can't tell themselves apart. None can say, I'm the juice of that tree, I'm the juice of this one. In the same way, all these creatures, when they merge into Being, don't know that they have merged. Then a line that keeps the picture honest. Whatever they are here, a tiger, a lion, a wolf, a boar, a worm, a moth, a gnat, a mosquito, that they become again. So the honey isn't everything blurring into mush. The tiger comes back a tiger, the gnat a gnat. What the bees show is something underneath the differences: a sweetness all of them share and no one of them owns. Then the refrain again. That which is the finest essence, this whole world has that as its self. That is the real. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. And again the son says: teach me more. Hold that next to the group project. The finished thing belongs to everyone and to no one alone, and the people who made it stay exactly who they are.
screen: `MANY TREES, ONE HONEY.` · `NO DROP SAYS: I'M FROM THAT TREE.` · `THE TIGER IS STILL A TIGER.` · then, large: `ONE SWEETNESS, NOBODY'S ALONE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you ate or used today, and count the hands behind it: who grew it, carried it, cooked it, sold it. Give each one a moment, each with a face, each exactly who they are. Then rest on the sweetness they made together.
Tat tvam asi: that you are. In the honey, the juices of many trees become one, and the father says it again.
Hold onto this: tat tvam asi, many flowers, one sweetness, and every tiger still a tiger. Day 1755, done.

screen: `DAY 1755 COUNTS.` → `TAT TVAM ASI · 4 OF 9.` → `TOMORROW: WHERE DO OPPOSITE RIVERS END UP?`

howItsDone: In Vedanta study, the honey, the rivers, the tree and the other pictures of Chandogya 6 are read one by one, each closing on the refrain tat tvam asi.

original.note: Sanskrit: honey. The father's picture for one essence beneath many beings.

trapdoor: what you thought: oneness means everyone blurs into one.
what it means: many juices become one honey, yet the tiger comes back a tiger.
what a scholar hears: 6.9.3, whatever they are here, tiger or lion or gnat, that they become again (tad abhavanti): difference kept, essence shared.

chat.meaning: In the honey, no juice can say 'I'm from this tree.' The mural is shared, and each painter still stays who they are.

Uddalaka.meaning: the father teaching his son in the Chandogya

Shvetaketu.meaning: the son who keeps asking to be taught more

tat tvam asi.meaning: that you are: the refrain after each picture

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 6.9.1–4 (as bees make honey by gathering the juices of many trees and bringing them to one, and the juices cannot tell 'I am the juice of this tree, of that tree', so all creatures merged in Being do not know they have merged; whatever they are here, tiger, lion, wolf, boar, worm, moth, gnat, mosquito, that they become again; that which is the finest essence ... that you are, Shvetaketu; please, sir, teach me more)

notes: The creature list follows the usual reading of 6.9.3 (vyaghra, simha, vrika, varaha, kita, patanga, damsha, mashaka); confirm the English names.
'The tiger comes back a tiger' is the lesson's gloss on 'that they become again'; confirm it is fair to the text across schools.
The group-project frame and the closing line of the teach are the lesson's application, not the text's; confirm they don't shrink the passage.
